  1. defLax330177.Representations

    Three representations of temporal graphs

    A finite lifetime includes empty snapshots. Chronological lists enumerate distinct arc occurrences. Ties can be permuted. Undirected edges have both orientations.

    • Snapshots to labels and back. Starting from snapshots, collecting the appearance times of each arc and reconstructing the snapshots recovers the original graph, including its lifetime.
    • Labels to snapshots and back. Starting from a time-labelled footprint, taking its snapshots and collecting the labels again recovers the original footprint, label sets, and lifetime.
    • Events and adjacency. At every time t, the snapshot reconstructed from the chronological event list contains the arc from u to v exactly when the original snapshot at t contains that arc.
    • Recovering an event list. Converting a chronological event list to snapshots and back preserves every event with its multiplicity. Only the order of events at the same time can change.
    • Snapshot adjacency and edge labels. An arc is active at time t exactly when its label set contains t.

    27 ∀ t u v, G.edge t u v ↔ G.edge t v u

    30inductive Direction where

    38def TimeLE (mode : TraversalMode) (a b : ℕ) : Prop :=

    43def ValidDirection {n : ℕ} (d : Direction) (G : Graph n) : Prop :=

    50/-- Explicit footprint and finite labels, with no unused footprint edges. -/
    51structure LabeledGraph (n : ℕ) where
    52 lifetime : ℕ
    53 footprint : Fin n → Fin n → Prop
    54 labels : Fin n → Fin n → Finset (Fin lifetime)
    55 supported : ∀ u v, footprint u v ↔ (labels u v).Nonempty
    56 loopless : ∀ u, ¬ footprint u u

    58def toLabels {n : ℕ} (G : Graph n) : LabeledGraph n where
    59 lifetime := G.lifetime
    60 footprint := Footprint G
    61 labels u v := Finset.univ.filter (fun t => G.edge t u v)
    62 supported := by intro u v; simp [Footprint, Finset.Nonempty]
    63 loopless := by intro u ⟨t, h⟩; exact G.loopless t u h

    65def LabeledGraph.toSnapshots {n : ℕ} (G : LabeledGraph n) : Graph n where
    66 lifetime := G.lifetime
    67 edge t u v := t ∈ G.labels u v
    68 loopless := by
    69 intro t u h
    70 exact G.loopless u ((G.supported u u).mpr ⟨t, h⟩)

    75structure EventStream (n h : ℕ) where
    76 events : List (Fin h × Fin n × Fin n)
    77 chronological : events.Pairwise (fun a b => a.1 ≤ b.1)
    78 unique : events.Nodup
    79 loopless : ∀ e ∈ events, e.2.1 ≠ e.2.2

    81def EventStream.snapshots {n h} (s : EventStream n h) : Graph n where
    82 lifetime := h
    83 edge t u v := (t,u,v) ∈ s.events

    88def occurrences {n} (G : Graph n) :=

    91def streamOf {n} (G : Graph n) : EventStream n G.lifetime := by
    92 let xs := (occurrences G).toList
    93 let cmp (a b : Fin G.lifetime × Fin n × Fin n) := decide (a.1 ≤ b.1)
    94 refine ⟨xs.mergeSort cmp, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    95 · have h := List.pairwise_mergeSort (le := cmp)
    96 (by simpa [cmp] using (fun a b c => @le_trans _ _ a.1 b.1 c.1 : ∀ a b c : Fin G.lifetime × Fin n × Fin n, _))
    97 (by intro a b; simpa [cmp] using le_total a.1 b.1) xs
    98 simpa [cmp] using h
    99 · exact (List.mergeSort_perm xs cmp).nodup_iff.mpr (Finset.nodup_toList _)
    100 · rintro ⟨t,u,v⟩ he huv
    101 change u = v at huv
    102 subst v
    103 exact G.loopless t u (by simpa [xs, occurrences] using he)

    lem✓Lax330177.SnapshotsLabels

    Fix a time and an ordered pair of vertices. The label set of that pair contains the time exactly when the original snapshot contains the arc. Reconstructing the snapshot tests this same membership, so it recovers every arc at every time. The lifetime is copied as well, even when the final snapshot is empty.

  4. defLax330177.Settings

    Temporal graph settings

    A setting selects direction, traversal mode and restrictions on the labelling. At a fixed time, two composable arcs u → v and v → w may coexist only when w = u. Opposite arcs may share a time, as may arcs with a common tail or a common head. For symmetric snapshots this is exactly the matching condition. Happy graphs are both simple and proper.

    14attribute [local instance] Classical.propDecidable
    15/-- Identity of the static edge, respecting the selected direction convention. -/
    16def SameStaticEdge (d : Direction) {n : ℕ} (u v x y : Fin n) : Prop :=
    17 match d with
    18 | .directed => u = x ∧ v = y
    19 | .undirected => (u = x ∧ v = y) ∨ (u = y ∧ v = x)
    20def IsSimple {n : ℕ} (G : Graph n) : Prop :=
    21 ∀ u v t s, G.edge t u v → G.edge s u v → t = s
    22
    23def IsProper {n : ℕ} (d : Direction) (G : Graph n) : Prop :=
    24 ValidDirection d G ∧ ∀ t u v w, G.edge t u v → G.edge t v w → u = w
    25
    26def IsHappy {n : ℕ} (d : Direction) (G : Graph n) : Prop :=
    27 IsSimple G ∧ IsProper d G
    28
    29def LabelMultiplicityBound {n : ℕ} (G : Graph n) (b : ℕ) : Prop :=
    30 ∀ u v, ((toLabels G).labels u v).card ≤ b
    31
    32structure Setting where
    33 direction : Direction
    34 mode : TraversalMode
    35 requireSimple : Bool := false
    36 requireProper : Bool := false
    37
    38def Setting.Admits {n : ℕ} (s : Setting) (G : Graph n) : Prop :=
    39 ValidDirection s.direction G ∧ (s.requireSimple = true → IsSimple G) ∧
    40 (s.requireProper = true → IsProper s.direction G)
    41
    42structure InterpretedGraph (n : ℕ) (s : Setting) where
    43 graph : Graph n
    44 admitted : s.Admits graph

  5. defLax330177.Paths

    Paths, walks and reachability

    Walks may revisit vertices. Paths have injective vertex sequences. Departure times increase strictly or weakly according to the traversal mode.

    • Walks and paths have the same reachability. In either traversal mode, a temporal walk from u to v exists exactly when a temporal path from u to v exists.
    • Strict paths give nonstrict reachability. If u can reach v by a strict temporal path, then u can also reach v by a nonstrict temporal path in the same graph.
    • Departure times on a proper graph. On a proper directed or undirected graph, every nonstrict temporal path already has strictly increasing departure times.
    • Reachability on a proper graph. On a proper directed or undirected graph, u reaches v strictly exactly when u reaches v nonstrictly.
    • Replacing undirected edges by opposite arcs. Replacing each undirected edge occurrence by both directed orientations preserves exactly the same timed paths of every length in the chosen traversal mode.
    • Path supports determine reachability. If two graphs on the same vertices realize exactly the same ordered vertex sequences as temporal paths in their respective modes, then they have the same reachability relation.
    • Temporal reachability is reflexive. Every vertex reaches itself in both modes, including at lifetime zero.
    • Enlarging the allowed vertex set. A path restricted to C remains feasible in any vertex superset D.
    • Allowing all vertices. Restricting the path to the full vertex set recovers ordinary temporal reachability.
    • Paths are static-edge trails. A vertex-simple path never uses a footprint edge twice, even counting reverse traversals as the same undirected edge.
    • Static-edge trails are temporal-edge trails. A walk that never repeats a static edge never repeats an edge-time occurrence.
    • Strict walks are temporal-edge trails. A strict walk never repeats an edge-time occurrence.
    • Properness of symmetric snapshots. On symmetric snapshots, directed properness is equivalent to undirected properness.

    30attribute [local instance] Classical.propDecidable
    31structure Walk {n : ℕ} (G : Graph n) (mode : TraversalMode) (k : ℕ) where
    32 vertex : Fin (k + 1) → Fin n
    33 time : Fin k → Fin G.lifetime
    34 available : ∀ i, G.edge (time i) (vertex i.castSucc) (vertex i.succ)
    35 ordered : ∀ i j, i < j → TimeLE mode (time i).val (time j).val
    36
    37namespace Walk
    38variable {n k : ℕ} {G : Graph n} {mode : TraversalMode}
    39
    40def start (w : Walk G mode k) := w.vertex 0
    41def finish (w : Walk G mode k) := w.vertex (Fin.last k)
    42def support (w : Walk G mode k) := List.ofFn w.vertex
    43def IsPath (w : Walk G mode k) : Prop := Function.Injective w.vertex
    44def IsStaticEdgeTrail (d : Direction) (w : Walk G mode k) : Prop :=
    45 ∀ i j : Fin k, SameStaticEdge d (w.vertex i.castSucc) (w.vertex i.succ)
    46 (w.vertex j.castSucc) (w.vertex j.succ) → i = j
    47def IsTemporalEdgeTrail (d : Direction) (w : Walk G mode k) : Prop :=
    48 ∀ i j : Fin k, SameStaticEdge d (w.vertex i.castSucc) (w.vertex i.succ)
    49 (w.vertex j.castSucc) (w.vertex j.succ) → w.time i = w.time j → i = j
    50
    51def StaysIn (w : Walk G mode k) (C : Finset (Fin n)) : Prop := ∀ i, w.vertex i ∈ C
    52def InWindow (w : Walk G mode k) (a b : ℕ) : Prop :=
    53 ∀ i, a ≤ (w.time i).val ∧ (w.time i).val < b
    54def IsClosed (w : Walk G mode k) : Prop := w.start = w.finish
    55def IsCircuit (d : Direction) (w : Walk G mode k) : Prop :=
    56 0 < k ∧ w.IsClosed ∧ w.IsStaticEdgeTrail d
    57/-- Positive closed walk without repeated vertices except the final return.
    58Undirected cycles also have at least three edges, directed cycles at least two. -/
    59def IsCycle (d : Direction) (w : Walk G mode k) : Prop :=
    60 (match d with | .directed => 2 ≤ k | .undirected => 3 ≤ k) ∧
    61 w.IsClosed ∧ Function.Injective (fun i : Fin k => w.vertex i.castSucc)
    62
    63def nil (G : Graph n) (mode : TraversalMode) (v : Fin n) : Walk G mode 0 where
    64 vertex _ := v
    65 time := Fin.elim0
    66 available := by intro i; exact Fin.elim0 i
    67 ordered := by intro i; exact Fin.elim0 i
    68
    69
    70def forgetStrict (w : Walk G .strict k) : Walk G .nonstrict k where
    71 vertex := w.vertex
    72 time := w.time
    73 available := w.available
    74 ordered := by intro i j h; exact Nat.le_of_lt (w.ordered i j h)
    75
    76
    77
    78
    79
    80
    81
    82/-- A contiguous segment, including its two endpoints. -/
    83def segment (w : Walk G mode k) (a len : ℕ) (h : a + len ≤ k) :
    84 Walk G mode len where
    85 vertex i := w.vertex ⟨a + i.val, by omega⟩
    86 time i := w.time ⟨a + i.val, by omega⟩
    87 available i := w.available ⟨a + i.val, by omega⟩
    88 ordered := by intro i j hij; apply w.ordered; change a + i.val < a + j.val; omega
    89
    90def take (w : Walk G mode k) (len : ℕ) (h : len ≤ k) := w.segment 0 len (by omega)
    91def suffix (w : Walk G mode k) (a : ℕ) (h : a ≤ k) :=
    92 w.segment a (k - a) (by omega)
    93
    94/-- Boundary condition for concatenation; empty operands impose no time constraint. -/
    95def CanAppend {l : ℕ} (w : Walk G mode k) (z : Walk G mode l) : Prop :=
    96 w.finish = z.start ∧ ∀ i j, TimeLE mode (w.time i).val (z.time j).val

    98end Walk

    100def Reaches {n : ℕ} (G : Graph n) (mode : TraversalMode) (u v : Fin n) : Prop :=
    101 ∃ k, ∃ w : Walk G mode k, w.IsPath ∧ w.start = u ∧ w.finish = v
    102def WalkReaches {n : ℕ} (G : Graph n) (mode : TraversalMode) (u v : Fin n) : Prop :=
    103 ∃ k, ∃ w : Walk G mode k, w.start = u ∧ w.finish = v
    104def ReachesIn {n : ℕ} (G : Graph n) (mode : TraversalMode)
    105 (C : Finset (Fin n)) (u v : Fin n) : Prop :=
    106 ∃ k, ∃ w : Walk G mode k, w.IsPath ∧ w.StaysIn C ∧ w.start = u ∧ w.finish = v
    107def ReachesDuring {n : ℕ} (G : Graph n) (mode : TraversalMode)
    108 (a b : ℕ) (u v : Fin n) : Prop :=
    109 ∃ k, ∃ w : Walk G mode k, w.IsPath ∧ w.InWindow a b ∧ w.start = u ∧ w.finish = v

    118abbrev StrictPath {n} (G : Graph n) := TemporalPath G .strict
    119abbrev NonstrictPath {n} (G : Graph n) := TemporalPath G .nonstrict
    120abbrev StrictReachability {n} (G : Graph n) := Reaches G .strict

  6. defLax330177.ReachabilityGraph

    The temporal reachability graph

    Fix a traversal mode. The reachability graph is the static directed graph on the original vertex set with an arc from u to v exactly when u and v are distinct and a temporal path in that mode goes from u to v. Each arc records a whole journey. Even undirected temporal graphs can have asymmetric reachability. The zero-edge path witnesses reflexivity of the relation, while the graph omits diagonal arcs.

    Strict and nonstrict reachability graphs on proper graphs.

    21def reachabilityGraph {n : ℕ} (G : Graph n) (mode : TraversalMode) : Digraph (Fin n) where
    22 Adj u v := u ≠ v ∧ Reaches G mode u v
    23
    24def ofSetting {n : ℕ} {s : Setting} (G : InterpretedGraph n s) : Digraph (Fin n) :=
    25 reachabilityGraph G.graph s.mode

  8. ⊢Lax330177Proofs.Basic.proper_path_times

    no assumptions

    →
    lem✓Lax330177.ProperPathTimes

    Consecutive steps have the form u → v → w with u and w distinct because the path never repeats a vertex. Properness forbids equal departure times for these two steps. Since the times are already weakly increasing, each is strictly smaller than its successor.

    thm✓Lax330177.ProperModes

    A strict path also satisfies the nonstrict timing rule. For the converse, take a nonstrict path. Consecutive edges form a two-step path with distinct outer vertices. Properness prevents both steps from using the same time. Their weakly increasing times must therefore increase strictly, giving a strict path with the same endpoints.

  13. defLax330177.Durations

    Traversal times

    Each occurrence has a natural traversal time. The next departure may occur at arrival. The lifetime bounds departure times and the final arrival may fall outside it.

    • Feasible departure times. For integer timestamps, a departure sequence is feasible with traversal time zero exactly when it is weakly increasing. With traversal time one, it is feasible exactly when it is strictly increasing.
    • The same timed paths. Fix the vertex sequence and every departure time. They form a path with uniform traversal time zero exactly when they form a nonstrict temporal path, and with uniform time one exactly when they form a strict temporal path.
    • The same reachable pairs. For every pair of vertices, reachability with uniform traversal time zero is equivalent to nonstrict reachability, and reachability with uniform time one is equivalent to strict reachability.

    2import Lax330177.Representations
    3import Lax330177.Paths

    17open Lax330177.Representations
    18open Lax330177.Paths
    19noncomputable section
    20attribute [local instance] Classical.propDecidable
    21
    22def Feasible {k : ℕ} (time duration : Fin k → ℕ) : Prop :=
    23 ∀ i j, i < j → time i + duration i ≤ time j
    24
    25def DurationPath {n k} (G : Graph n) (δ : Fin G.lifetime → Fin n → Fin n → ℕ)
    26 (x : Fin (k+1) → Fin n) (t : Fin k → Fin G.lifetime) : Prop :=
    27 Function.Injective x ∧ (∀ i, G.edge (t i) (x i.castSucc) (x i.succ)) ∧
    28 Feasible (fun i => (t i).val) (fun i => δ (t i) (x i.castSucc) (x i.succ))
    29
    30
    31def DurationReaches {n} (G : Graph n) (δ : Fin G.lifetime → Fin n → Fin n → ℕ)
    32 (u v : Fin n) : Prop :=
    33 ∃ k, ∃ x : Fin (k+1) → Fin n, ∃ t : Fin k → Fin G.lifetime,
    34 DurationPath G δ x t ∧ x 0 = u ∧ x (Fin.last k) = v
    35
    36
    37
    38end
    39end Lax330177.Durations

    The same timed paths

    Fix the vertex sequence and every departure time. They form a path with uniform traversal time zero exactly when they form a nonstrict temporal path, and with uniform time one exactly when they form a strict temporal path.

    Read the proof.

    17axiom uniform_paths {n k} (G : Graph n) (m : TraversalMode) (x : Fin (k+1) → Fin n) (t : Fin k → Fin G.lifetime) : DurationPath G (fun _ _ _ => if m = .strict then 1 else 0) x t ↔ ∃ w : TemporalPath G m k, w.val.vertex = x ∧ w.val.time = t
    18end Lax330177.UniformPaths

  15. ⊢Lax330177Proofs.Basic.uniform_paths

    no assumptions

    →
    lem✓Lax330177.UniformPaths

    Fix the vertex sequence and its departure times. Both path definitions require distinct vertices and an available edge at every departure. For uniform time zero, arrival before or at the next departure means that departure times are weakly increasing. For uniform time one, it means that the integer times are strictly increasing. Thus the same sequences satisfy either description exactly in the stated mode.

  16. defLax330177.OptimalPaths

    Optimal temporal paths

    Fix two vertices, traversal times, a release time and an inclusive arrival deadline. A shortest path minimizes traversals. A fastest path minimizes elapsed time from first departure to final arrival. Foremost paths minimize arrival, and latest departure paths maximize departure. Minimum waiting paths minimize the sum of idle gaps at internal vertices. Initial waiting and time after arrival do not contribute. A zero-edge path occupies its vertex at any one instant in the window. Every feasible query admits an optimizer for each of the five criteria.

    • Each objective attains its optimum. Fix the endpoints, traversal times, release time and arrival deadline. If at least one feasible path exists, then each of the five criteria has an optimal path. The optimizing path may depend on the criterion.
    1import Lax330177.Durations
    2import Mathlib.Order.Filter.Extr
    3import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Group.Finset.Basic
    4
    … module docstring, 15 lines
    20namespace Lax330177.OptimalPaths
    21open Lax330177.Representations Lax330177.Durations
    22
    23structure Query {n : ℕ} (G : Graph n) where
    24 source : Fin n
    25 target : Fin n
    26 release : ℕ
    27 deadline : ℕ
    28 transit : Fin G.lifetime → Fin n → Fin n → ℕ
    29
    30variable {n : ℕ} {G : Graph n} (q : Query G)
    31
    32structure Candidate where
    33 hops : ℕ
    34 vertex : Fin (hops+1) → Fin n
    35 time : Fin hops → Fin G.lifetime
    36 feasible : DurationPath G q.transit vertex time
    37 starts : vertex 0 = q.source
    38 ends : vertex (Fin.last hops) = q.target
    39 departure : ℕ
    40 arrival : ℕ
    41 released : q.release ≤ departure
    42 inOrder : departure ≤ arrival
    43 onTime : arrival ≤ q.deadline
    44 first : ∀ h : 0 < hops, departure = (time ⟨0,h⟩).val
    45 last : ∀ h : 0 < hops,
    46 let i : Fin hops := ⟨hops-1, by omega⟩
    47 arrival = (time i).val + q.transit (time i) (vertex i.castSucc) (vertex i.succ)
    48 instantaneous : hops = 0 → departure = arrival
    49
    50variable {q}
    51def Candidate.elapsed (p : Candidate q) := p.arrival - p.departure
    52
    53def Candidate.waiting (p : Candidate q) : ℕ :=
    54 ∑ i : Fin p.hops, if h : i.val + 1 < p.hops then
    55 (p.time ⟨i.val+1,h⟩).val - ((p.time i).val + q.transit (p.time i) (p.vertex i.castSucc) (p.vertex i.succ))
    56 else 0
    57
    58def Shortest (p : Candidate q) := IsMinOn Candidate.hops Set.univ p
    59def Fastest (p : Candidate q) := IsMinOn Candidate.elapsed Set.univ p
    60def Foremost (p : Candidate q) := IsMinOn Candidate.arrival Set.univ p
    61abbrev EarliestArrival (p : Candidate q) := Foremost p
    62def LatestDeparture (p : Candidate q) := IsMaxOn Candidate.departure Set.univ p
    63def MinimumWaiting (p : Candidate q) := IsMinOn Candidate.waiting Set.univ p
    64
    65end Lax330177.OptimalPaths
    66
    67
  17. thm✓Lax330177.ElapsedEq

    Elapsed time splits into travel and waiting

    If every available traversal takes c time units, every feasible path has elapsed time equal to its total internal waiting time plus c times its number of hops.

    Read the proof.

    1import Lax330177.UniformCosts
    2
    … module docstring, 9 lines
    12namespace Lax330177.ElapsedEq
    13open Lax330177.Representations Lax330177.OptimalPaths
    14open Lax330177.UniformCosts
    15variable {n : ℕ} {G : Graph n} {q : Query G}
    16
    17axiom elapsed_eq (p : Candidate q) (c : ℕ) (h : Uniform q c) :
    18 p.elapsed = p.waiting + p.hops * c
    19end Lax330177.ElapsedEq
    20
  18. ⊢Lax330177Proofs.UniformCosts.elapsed_eq

    no assumptions

    →
    thm✓Lax330177.ElapsedEq

    Split the interval from first departure to final arrival into the traversals and the gaps between them. Each traversal contributes c time units. Each gap runs from one arrival to the next departure and contributes exactly the waiting time there. These pieces cover the interval in order, so elapsed time equals total waiting plus c times the hop count. A zero-hop path departs and arrives at the same instant, making both sides zero.

  19. lem✓Lax330177.ZeroOptima

    Zero traversal time

    With uniform traversal time zero, a feasible path is fastest exactly when it minimizes total internal waiting time.

  20. ⊢Lax330177Proofs.UniformCosts.zero_optima
    • thm✓Lax330177.ElapsedEq
    →
    lem✓Lax330177.ZeroOptima

    Set c to zero in the elapsed-time identity. Every path then has elapsed time equal to its own waiting time. Consequently two feasible paths compare in exactly the same order under the two criteria, including ties, and their sets of minimizers coincide.

  21. lem✓Lax330177.NoWaitDetour

    A detour with no waiting

    On the three-vertex chain and its shortcut triangle, each traversal takes c units, where c is zero or one. In the triangle, the two-hop path departing at 0 and c minimizes waiting for either traversal cost and uses more hops than the shortcut. It is fastest exactly when c is zero.

  22. ⊢Lax330177Proofs.CostExamples.no_wait_detour

    no assumptions

    →
    lem✓Lax330177.NoWaitDetour

    Depart on the two arcs at times 0 and c. The second departure is exactly the first arrival, so total waiting is zero, the least possible. The direct arc uses one hop instead of two. With c equal to zero the detour also takes zero elapsed time and is fastest. With c equal to one it takes two units, while the direct arc takes only one.
